> **Paths in this skill.** `<plugin-root>` is this plugin's own folder, the folder two levels above the folder this SKILL.md sits in. In Claude Code it is also `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. `<merlin-data>` is your business folder, `${user_config.data_dir}`; where that is empty or still reads as written, use the `data_root` value in `~/.merlin/instance.json`. Write both as absolute paths in every command you run, because a shell cannot expand either one.

# Save and close

Close the current session with its state safely recorded. Closing a session
does not mean all its work is complete. Keep unfinished work open and easy to
pick up again.

## Scope and authority

Run on an explicit request to close the session, including the older names
"wrap-session" and "wrap session". A request to edit or discuss this skill
does not close anything. Bare "save", "done with X" and checkpoint requests do
not run it. When a session that changed things winds down, a one-line offer
to save and close is enough; run only after a yes, and do not offer again
once the bookkeeping is done.

A checkpoint keeps unfinished work safe during a long session and never
closes it. For a checkpoint, or to continue the work in a fresh session, read
[continuation.md](continuation.md) instead.

The closing request covers ordinary session bookkeeping inside the Merlin
data folder. It never covers sending, publishing, deleting, spending, or
skipping an approval the user has not given, just to make the session look
finished. If the user asked to preview before writing, preview. A blocked
write is reported as blocked and earns no success line.

If the business folder cannot be reached, write nothing, say why, and give
the user the state to save by hand. That is not a successful close. If no business folder is chosen yet, tell the user to run `/merlin:setup`, which asks for one.

## 1. Find the project and save the session

Work out which project this session belongs to: the folder the session was
opened in, inside `<merlin-data>`. Read its `CONTINUITY.md` and only the task
lines and files this session touched. If the project has no `CONTINUITY.md`
and is not brand new, or the project is unclear, stop and ask. For a brand
new project, create `CONTINUITY.md` with the five sections in § The
CONTINUITY file below.

From this session, collect: decisions and why, verified results, current
state, unfinished work, blockers, approvals already given, and where the
evidence is. Keep built, tested, staged and live apart. A step only a person
can do (publishing, sending, deploying) stays open even when all the local
work is finished.

If nothing durable changed (no state, no decision, no open obligation), write
nothing. Check that against the conversation and report "Read-only session;
no writes needed." That is a successful close. A read-only session that
produced a decision or a follow-up did change something, and saves it.

Otherwise:

1. Update the current-state, open-loops and next-move parts of
   `CONTINUITY.md`, and its `**Last updated:**` date.
2. Write or update one dated session log in the project's `updates/` folder,
   named `YYYY-MM-DD_<short-topic>.md`. Reuse this session's log if it
   already exists; never write the same entry twice on a retry.
3. Keep the header to one dated line. Before replacing `**Last updated:**`,
   move the outgoing line, word for word, to the top of `## Session log`.
4. `## Current state` holds open and in-progress work only. Move every line
   this session finished, word for word, into `## Session log` under this
   session's entry. If a finished line names follow-on work that is still
   open, leave one line naming that follow-on and its task id. Never reword,
   merge or drop a moved line, and leave other sessions' lines alone.

Record one resume pointer: the project name, its folder, where the full state
is, and the next action someone could run cold. If no work remains, say so
and do not invent a task.

Immediately before writing, re-read the sections you are about to change and
compare them with what you composed. If they changed since you read them,
recompose. Keep other sessions' changes intact.

## 2. Update this session's tasks

Use `merlin:task-management` for every task change. It runs the task engine;
never hand-edit `<merlin-data>/TASKS.md`. Match tasks by id and by what they
actually ask for. Reuse an open task for the same obligation.

- **Close** only work this session fully finished, with evidence. Append the
  evidence before closing. Built but still waiting on a check, a review, an
  approval or a delivery stays open.
- **Annotate** partial progress: what landed and the exact remaining step.
  Leave the checkbox open. If you are not sure a task matches, leave it open
  and say so.
- **Add** new obligations this session created, tagged with their project,
  with the state file and the exact next action in the description.
- A step only a person can do gets a task too, saying what is ready and what
  they still have to do. Other next steps stay in `CONTINUITY.md` rather
  than becoming duplicate tasks.

## 3. Check the writes

Read every changed section and every task result back from disk. Confirm the
date, decisions, open work, resume pointer and task status against the
evidence. Check each engine result, not only its exit status: a skipped
change is not a successful one. Fix this session's mistakes; report problems
that were already there without trying to fix unrelated work.

Check the deliverables this session created or changed: the right template,
any companion file the project requires, and that a companion matches its
current source. A missing or blocked deliverable stays an open obligation.

Close only temporary things this session opened (a preview, a scratch file),
and leave open anything the user asked to keep or is still reading. Do not
audit the rest of the project, other tasks, calendars or other sessions.

## 4. Confirm briefly

Give a short outcome, the path to the saved state or session log, the task
changes, and the project and next action when work remains. State any
blocked write plainly. No file-by-file list in chat, no follow-on session
offer.

Only after the save writes are verified, or the read-only no-op is verified,
end with this exact final line, with nothing after it:

✅ Session saved and closed.

## The CONTINUITY file

Used only when a brand-new project has none. Sections, in this order:

```markdown
# CONTINUITY.md · <Project>

**Last updated:** <YYYY-MM-DD> (<what happened>)

## Current state
## Open loops
## Risks and blockers
## Best next move
## Session log
```

The session log stays last, newest entry first, one entry per line.
